answer.rationale: Timeline is the strongest signal available: the release landed 2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90m ago, which is consistent with a release-induced regression rather than pure load (settlement peak is a recurring, previously-absorbed pattern per memory_b3, and capacity work is a next-window action anyway). memory_b2 explicitly rules out regional_failover here — writes are hot, and that memory records lost customer writes and a 40-minute replication gap; that directly conflicts with the primary objective of not losing writes. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) addressed read/report load stealing primary capacity, which is a different failure shape than a post-deploy write-path regression, though it stays as the fallback if verification undercuts the release hypothesis. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained an external partner outage; nothing here indicates a downstream dependency failing. So I intend rollback_release. I want the archived source for memory_b1 because it is the sole basis for the action and the consolidated summary ('rollback finished without customer impact') may have flattened whether that rollback happened during heavy write load or during a quiet window — a rollback that was safe at low write volume is not evidence it is safe at settlement peak, especially if the release carried a schema or data-format migration that a rollback would strand. I want memory_b6 because it tells me whether staged/canary gating is actually wired up here; if canary cohorts surfaced regressions within an hour before, then a cohort-scoped rollback is both feasible and a fast causal test. Hence small_guarded_test: roll back on one canary cohort first, watch write p99 and error rates on that cohort against the unchanged fleet, and only widen if the signal separates. Downstream value risk is real and flagged — any writes accepted under the new build could be in a format the prior build cannot read, so before widening I check for migrations in the release and, if present, treat rollback as unsafe and fall back to route_read_replicas to shed primary load. I am not treating the release as confirmed cause; correlation in timing is suggestive, not conclusive, and the guarded scale exists precisely so a wrong hypothesis is cheap.
